name: EU AI Act — Article 13 (Transparency and Provision of Information)
scope: High-risk AI systems placed on the EU market
summary: High-risk AI systems must be designed so that their operation is sufficiently transparent to enable deployers to interpret and use the system output, including a complete description of model provenance, input data, decision logic, and confidence scoring.

requirements.title: Intended purpose and capability disclosure
requirements.description: The AI system must carry machine-readable metadata declaring its intended purpose, capabilities, and known limitations.

requirements.title: Provenance of training and operational data
requirements.description: Every AI decision must be traceable to input data with full PROV-O provenance, including agent attribution and derivation method.

requirements.title: Confidence scoring and derivation transparency
requirements.description: Each AI output must carry a confidence score and derivation method that an auditor can read.

requirements.title: Structural validation of AI outputs
requirements.description: AI-generated observations must be validated against a SHACL acceptance shape before they enter the reasoning scope.

requirements.title: PROV-O decision chain for the specific decision under audit
requirements.description: For the decision identified in the evidence query, the full PROV-O chain from source data to agent attribution must be retrievable.

requirements.title: Low-confidence output flagging
requirements.description: Decisions below 0.8 confidence must be discoverable via SPARQL so deployers can review before acting.
